outcomes: A TypeScript author binds an ordinary bun test to a declared check without changing how the test is written or what it returns
The verification wire receives what the runner observed, so a spec gate resolves TypeScript evidence exactly as it resolves Go and Python evidence
A repository that does not run the Putnami test adapter keeps its suite byte-for-byte unchanged
nonGoals: Deciding a verdict: the fragment states an observation and core recomputes every verdict against the authored criterion
Validating, attributing, or merging fragments — the test adapter owns all three
Supporting test runners other than bun

requirements.text: specTest and observeMeasurement wrap bun:test and never change the verdict the runner gives: a suite whose bound body fails still fails, with or without a fragment directory. The fragment they write is the features protocol's, which @putnami/spectest proves under features/feature-contracts.
